newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares forge ahead to a stronger close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares forge ahead to a stronger close.

text.p: The Zealand share market forged ahead to fresh 32-month highs on Thursday, closing 22.73 points stronger on healthy volume worth NZ$80.5 million.
The NZSE-40 Capital index, which hit 2,353.52 during the session, ended at 2,348.71. It has not seen these levels since February 1994.
"There's just on-going interest in the market from offshore players and from locals," said Stuart Christie of broker Hendry Hay McIntosh. "The belief is that the market will continue to firm up."
He said there was a lot of value in the market now that the uncertainty surrounding the October 12 election was reduced by the poor showing of the left-wing Alliance Party.

Despite the Reserve Bank's statement on Wednesday that it saw no scope for a further easing in monetary conditions, Christie said there was an expectation of an easing at some stage. "It may not happen before Christmas," he said.

Brokers said Telecom in particular was benefiting from investors reweighting into equities. The market leader was up nine cents to $7.40. Carter Holt Harvey was the other stand-out performer, up seven cents to $3.37.
Outside the leaders, Fletcher Building continued its impressive run, rising to a fresh high for the year of $3.89.
Publisher Wilson and Horton, currently the target of an NZ$11/share takeover bid from a subsidiary of Independent Newspapers Plc, rose 20 cents to $11.30.

"There's a lot of scepticism whether this bid is actually going to be successful," said Christie. "So they will let the bid lapse, wait a few months and then bid again at a higher price. People are coming to that realisation."
